To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
neurotrophin signaling induces nuclear translocalization of PCAF and GCN5 histone acetylases via phosphorylation-dependent activation of PI3-kinase/Rsk2pp90/MSK1 signaling.

NGF signaling induces histone acetyl-transferase domain-dependent nuclear translocation and activation of PCAF and GCN5 acetyl-transferases, which is required for p53-dependent transcriptional activation of the p21Waf1/Cip1 gene during NGF-induced neuronal differentiation.

nerve growth factor (NGF) induces nuclear translocation and histone acetylase activity of p300/ CREB-binding protein-associated Factor (PCAF) acetyltransferase and hGCN-5 histone acetyl-transferases, which are required for NGF-mediated p53 acetylation and transcriptional activation of p53-responsive genes during neuronal differentiation.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the molecular mechanism of transcriptional regulation of the cell cycle in the developing brain.
understanding how growth factor signals regulate the transcription of specific target genes.
the molecular mechanisms of signal transduction that modulate gene expression and cell growth and differentiation in neurons.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

neurotrophin receptor signaling induces nuclear acetylation of p53 by PCAF, which is dependent upon phosphorylation of Ser/Thr residues within the histone acetylase domains of PCAF and GCN5, and this process requires activation of PI 3-kinase, Rsk2, and MSK.

NGF receptor signaling induces nuclear accumulation of PCAF and GCN5 acetyl transferases via phosphorylation of the histone acetyl transferase domain, thereby promoting acetylation of p53 at Lys320 and activation of the p21Waf1/Cip1 promoter.
the phosphorylation of PCAF and p300 histone acetylase by the MAPK/ERK pathway is required for their nuclear translocation and for their transcriptional coactivator function.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
NGF induces the nuclear translocation of the histone acetyl transferases, p300/CBP-associated factor (PC AF) and hGCNs, in a PI3K/Rsk2/MSK-1-dependent manner.

NGF receptor signaling activates PI3K/Rsk2/MSK-1 signaling pathways, which in turn phosphorylate PCAF and hGcn5 at specific Ser and Thr residues, thereby inducing the nuclear translocation of these acetyltransferases, which then acetylate p53K320 and activate the expression of the p21Waf1/Cip1 gene, which in turn induces cell cycle arrest.
NGF receptor stimulation induces the nuclear translocation of the histone acetyl transferases (HATs), PCAF and hGcn5, which is dependent upon the phosphorylational state of the HAT domains.
The main takeaway from our work is that
neurotrophin receptor signals modulate histone acetylase nuclear translocation via phosphorylation of the acetyltransferase domain.

the nuclear translocation of the histone acetyl transferases PCAF and hGcn5 is regulated by phosphorylation of their acetyl transferase domains by MAPKs and that these histone acetylases are required for p53 activation in neurons.
neurotrophin receptor stimulation induces nuclear translocation, histone acetylation, and transcriptional activation of p21WAF1/CIP1 gene expression by the coactivators PCAF and hGNCS.
